name: data-file-viewer
description: Open and explore .duckdb, .parquet, .csv, .dta (Stata), .db/.sqlite (SQLite), and kdb+ data files right inside VS Code, without needing a separate database program. A sidebar lists every table in the file — click one to see its rows in a grid, or write your own SQL query to look at exactly the data you want. Click a column header to sort by it, or open the stats panel to see quick numbers for that column — minimum, maximum, average, and percentiles — worked out across the whole dataset, not just the rows on screen. For editable formats (.duckdb, .parquet, .csv, .dta, .db/.sqlite), double-click a cell to change its value and save it straight back to the file; turn on Safe Mode first to keep an automatic backup and see exactly which rows changed before you commit to the edit. kdb+ tables are read directly in their real, original format — no conversion step — though they are view-only for now, since there is no way yet to write changes back into that format.

dataFileViewer.diffRowThreshold.description: Above this many rows, automatic diff-against-backup highlighting is skipped after a query — use "Diff anyway" to run it on demand instead.

scripts.package: npm run build && npx vsce package
